content:
priya: Quick sync — after launch metrics, we need to lock the next 2-week iteration. TL;DR: 3 customer-facing bugs, 4 enhancement asks, +1 perf regression on embeddings. Need decisions on bugs vs enhancements and rollout plan :hourglass_flowing_sand:

matt: can we get severity + repro rate from support? dev estimates will be fuzzy without that.

josh: added a support summary in the ticket thread: https://redwood/jira/RI-482 — short: Bug-A high freq (~8% of requests), Bug-B intermittent, Bug-C small UI glitch. 3 paying customers flagged A.

kevin: quick numbers from analytics: Bug-A correlates with 8% of calls and increases median latency by ~40ms on affected requests. Perf regression (embedding model) shows 6% higher cost.

priya: proposing a lightweight prioritization formula we can apply to each item, so we don't just go by loudness: 
```
priority_score = (users_affected * severity_weight) / (dev_days + 0.5 * risk_factor)
severity_weight: P0=10, P1=6, P2=3
```
Use customer_weight multiplier (enterprise=1.5) when enterprise tickets involved.

matt: sounds fine. dev estimates: Bug-A ~ 2 dev-days (root cause likely path caching), Perf-regression ~ 4 dev-days to profile + revert plan, Streaming-UX enhancement ~ 6 dev-days.

priya: applying formula (very rough):
- Bug-A: users_affected=0.08, severity=P1(6), dev_days=2 => score ~ (0.08*6)/2=0.24 -> *enterprise 1.5 => 0.36
- Perf-regression: users_affected=0.06, severity=P1(6), dev_days=4 => 0.09
- Streaming UX: users_affected=0.12, severity=P2(3), dev_days=6 => 0.06
So ordered: Bug-A, perf-regression, streaming UX. (scores are relative; we care rank not absolute)

sara: from design POV, Bug-C (UI glitch) is quick fix (0.5 dev-days) and helps perception for new signups — would slot as quick-win if we have bandwidth.

emma: QA notes — for Bug-A we need a canary matrix: replicate with 10k synthetic calls + 5 customers in canary. Test plan will take ~2 QA-days. Also need regression tests for embeddings perf if we change quantization.

priya: rollout proposal:
- Hotfix patch for Bug-A: canary 5% -> 25% -> full (24h observation each) if metrics good. target ship: next Tue.
- Perf regression: create profiling branch, if root cause is quantization switch, default back to previous quant profile for Dedicated customers, and ship opt-in rollout for host users.
- Streaming UX: schedule for next minor after this patch wave.

matt: agree. If Bug-A fix is small, we can include Bug-C in same patch. Otherwise keep separate.

josh: I'll prep comms for the 3 enterprise customers and offer them the canary slot if they want immediate relief.

kevin: I'll add dashboards for the canary (latency, error-rate, tokens-per-request). Will set alert if latency delta > 20ms or error-rate > baseline + 0.5%.

priya: acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Bug-A: repro <0.1% on canary within 24h and no P0 regressions.
- Perf-regression: rolling revert reduces cost delta to <=1% vs baseline or we document tradeoff + opt-in toggle.
- Streaming UX: measurable completion rate increase or NPS signal in 2 weeks.

emma: QA will need test data and a short smoke script. I'll create a checklist in the ticket.

release-bot: Release pipeline scheduled: patch-build-2298766 queued for Tue 09:00 PT. Auto-canary configured at 5% for 6h, then 25% for 18h, rollback on alert.

priya: action items:
- matt: implement Bug-A fix + scope Bug-C as quick-win (if <1 day)
- emma: test plan + smoke scripts
- kevin: canary dashboards & alerts
- josh: enterprise comms + canary slots
- sara: short UX note for streaming changes (deferred if not in this patch)
- priya: finalize priorities and unblock devs by EOD

matt: I'll sync with infra about canary capacity. ETA on PR by Monday morning.

priya: thanks all — let's regroup Mon 10am to confirm PR status. :thumbsup:
